newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air names outsider Mullin president.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air names outsider Mullin president.

text.p: Delta Air Lines named Leo Mullin as its new president and chief executive officer Friday, marking the first time the nation's third-largest carrier hired an outsider as CEO.
Mullin, vice chairman of Chicago-based Unicom Corp., succeeds Ronald Allen, who left the carrier in July after 34 years with Delta when the board declined to renew his contract.
Mullin has a strong reputation for business strategy and extensive experience in highly competitive, consumer-oriented industries, Delta said.

Tapping an industry outsider will bring a fresh perspective to the airline as it seeks to boost employee morale and improve customer service, two areas hit by years of overly aggressive cost-cutting, analysts said.

"It was expected that they would pick someone from outside the company and someone from outside the industry, and they certainly did that," said Jeffrey Long, an airline analyst at J.P. Morgan Securities.
Long said the cost-cutting has hurt Delta's service and led to a loss of business travelers, who often fly on short notice and pay full fare, generating big profits for airlines.
But despite those problems, management at the carrier was sound. "They definitely know how to run an airline," he said.
Delta, based in Atlanta, also named Gerald Grinstein, a member of the airlines' board and head of the CEO search committee, as non-executive chairman of the board.
Maurice Worth, acting Delta CEO, was named chief operating officer. Mary Johnston Evans, acting chairman, was named chairman of the executive committee of the board.

"This new leadership gives Delta shareowners, employees and customers a mix of airline industry experience and a new and objective management approach with a proven record of achievement," Grinstein said.

Delta's pilots union said it was "cautiously optimistic" about the appointments. Although Mullin comes from outside the industry, "he does appear to meet a lot of the criteria," said Karen McGuffey, a spokeswoman for the Air Line Pilots Association at Delta.

"I'd imagine that there is a learning curve involved, but we're cautiously optimistic that his management and strategic planning skills may be strong enough to be applied to whatever industry he is in," she said.

"I think it's good they've gone outside the company to get somebody new, and I think it's good they named someone who's with the company for a long time as chief operating officer, for continuity," said Smith Barney analyst Helane Becker.
Before joining Unicom in 1995, Mullin was president of the Midwest bank First Chicago Corp. and had been involved with Conrail, the railroad in the Northeast.
"My goal is to build on Delta's foundation and further enhance shareowner value. A top priority will be to see Delta's true worth reflected in increased value for shareowners," Mullin said.
Delta stock rose 37.5 cents to $88.125 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
